title: Valid parentheses
prompt:
PageTurn's quiz builder lets teachers type math expressions such as {[(2+3)*4]-1}. Before saving, reject expressions whose brackets don't balance.

Write isBalanced(text) that returns true if every opener ( [ { is closed by the matching closer ) ] } in the right order, and false otherwise. Ignore every other character.

Examples:

  • isBalanced("{[(2+3)*4]-1}") → true
  • isBalanced("()[]{}") → true
  • isBalanced("([)]") → false (closed in the wrong order)
  • isBalanced("((") → false (never closed)
  • isBalanced("") → true

Constraints: 0 ≤ text.length ≤ 104.

tests.name: closer with nothing open
empty string and no brackets at all

hints: Every closer must match the most recent opener that is still open. "Most recent first" is last-in-first-out: a stack.
Walk the string. Push openers. On a closer: if the stack is empty, it's invalid; otherwise pop and check the popped opener is its partner. At the end, the stack must be empty.

Shape:

const partner = { ')': '(', ']': '[', '}': '{' };
const open = [];
for (const ch of text) {
  if ('([{'.includes(ch)) open.push(ch);
  else if (ch in partner) {
    if (open.length === 0 || open.pop() !== partner[ch]) return false;
  }
}
return open.length === 0;
explain:
Time O(n), space O(n) in the worst case (a string of only openers). Each character is pushed and popped at most once. The repeated-deletion approach is O(n²) because it rescans the whole string for every pair.

Parsers for JSON, HTML and programming languages use exactly this idea (often an explicit or implicit stack of what's currently open) to catch "unexpected token" errors.

In an interview: "Each closer has to match the most recent unmatched opener, so I'll use a stack: push openers, pop and compare on closers, and require an empty stack at the end. O(n) time, O(n) space."
